segments.text: > Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. `performance.*` can be implemented with a single `clock_gettime()` call. Includes `Date`, since real JS/Node group wall-clock timing APIs together too.

notes: Milliseconds since the program's **time origin** (process start), as a `double` (sub-millisecond precision) — the origin is captured once at process start by an `llvm.global_ctors` constructor, matching the spec's origin-relative reading ([ADR-00568](../adr/ADR-00568.md))
`CLOCK_MONOTONIC`-based — unlike `Date.now()`, not tied to wall-clock time
See [ADR-00024](../adr/ADR-00024.md)

caveats: Re-marking a name overwrites its timestamp — last-write-wins, not a full ordered entries list
`measure()` returns the elapsed milliseconds directly as a plain number rather than a `PerformanceMeasure` object, and its own `name` argument is evaluated but not stored anywhere
notes: Named timing marks backed by a `Map<string, number>`; no `getEntriesByName`/`PerformanceObserver` machinery exists for a `PerformanceMeasure` to belong to
`endMark` defaults to the current `performance.now()` reading when omitted
Measuring against a name that was never marked throws, matching real `performance.measure()`'s own behavior
See [ADR-00111](../adr/ADR-00111.md)

caveats: UTC-only everywhere (construction, getters, formatting) — a deliberate deviation from real JS's local-time default, for deterministic output regardless of the machine/CI timezone; the multi-argument constructor form is a special case of this: real JS treats its fields as *local* time, this compiler always treats them as UTC
notes: `new Date()` / `new Date(ms)` / `new Date(isoString)` (the string form parses via the same logic as `Date.parse`, including its `-1`-on-unparseable sentinel — see [ADR-00038](../adr/ADR-00038.md)) / `new Date(year, month, day?, hours?, minutes?, seconds?, ms?)` (month 0-indexed, matching `getMonth()`; omitted trailing fields default like real JS — day to 1, everything after that to 0; see [ADR-00039](../adr/ADR-00039.md))
`getFullYear/Month/Date/Day/Hours/Minutes/Seconds/Milliseconds`, `getTime`/`valueOf`, `toISOString`
See [ADR-00014](../adr/ADR-00014.md)
Milliseconds since epoch, via `clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, ...)`

caveats: Unparseable input returns `-1` (a documented sentinel — this compiler's Date has no NaN representation)
notes: ISO 8601 strings, with or without milliseconds: `Z` (UTC), a `+HH:MM`/`-HH:MM` timezone offset (converted to UTC), or a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` date
See [ADR-00015](../adr/ADR-00015.md) and [ADR-00017](../adr/ADR-00017.md)

caveats: Requires a named-variable receiver (not a field access or call result — this compiler's Date is a plain number, not a reference object, so there's no heap location to mutate otherwise)
notes: Mutate a named Date variable in place and return the new timestamp, matching real JS
See [ADR-00016](../adr/ADR-00016.md)
Multi-argument setter overloads cascade into the following fields (`setFullYear(y, m, d)`, `setHours(h, m, s, ms)`, …) ([ADR-00488](../adr/ADR-00488.md))

caveats: `Date ± number` gives a new Date (a deliberate deviation from real JS, where `+` on a Date string-concatenates instead — numeric duration arithmetic is far more useful for this compiler's plain-number Date representation)
`Date + Date`, `number - Date`, and compound-assigning a Date into a Date are all rejected at compile time
notes: `Date - Date` gives the difference in milliseconds (a number), matching real JS
See [ADR-00018](../adr/ADR-00018.md)
Fixed `"Www Mon DD YYYY"` shape (e.g. `"Thu Jan 01 1970"`), matching real JS exactly except for the UTC deviation
See [ADR-00019](../adr/ADR-00019.md)

caveats: One fixed `"M/D/YYYY"` format (the default en-US shape), always UTC; no locale argument or full `Intl`-style locale support
notes: See [ADR-00019](../adr/ADR-00019.md)
